Return real 404s instead of serving the app at 200

not_found_handling was "single-page-application", so every unmatched path
answered with the 214 KB index.html at HTTP 200. /vite/.env, /wp-admin/install.php
and every scraped typo became a 200-status duplicate of the homepage. Google
records those as soft 404s and spends crawl budget on them, and a scanner reads
200 as a probe worth repeating. app.shrinkr.in has been at 0 of 6 pages indexed
since mid-June, and this is the most likely reason.

The obvious fix, a _redirects file mapping the SPA routes to /index.html at
status 200, does not work on Workers Assets:

  Found 5 invalid redirect rules:
  Infinite loop detected in this rule and has been ignored.
    at _redirects:14 | /manage/*    /index.html    200

Rewrites are a Pages feature. So worker.js matches the six client-side routes
and serves the shell for those; everything else falls through to the asset
handler, which now serves 404.html with a real 404.

worker.js asks the asset binding for "/" rather than "/index.html": the
handler normalises an explicit /index.html back to / with a 307, which would
hand the browser a redirect and lose the requested path.

404.html keeps the courtesy redirect for app.shrinkr.in/<slug>, which route()
used to handle: crawlers get the 404, and only a browser that runs the script
follows the hop to shrinkr.in.

Verified locally against wrangler dev, 17 paths: SPA routes and guide pages 200,
scanner paths 404, robots.txt and sitemap.xml 200, worker.js not publicly
served, and the _headers CSP/HSTS rules still applied on both branches.

Also:
- robots.txt collapsed to one User-agent: * group.
- Oversized wordmark closing the footer.
